subject: Confirming regional custody constraints and DPA addendum for MedLumen
messages:
From: Sophie Moreau <sophie.moreau@medlumen-eu.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@medlumen-eu.com
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 16:12:00 +0200
Subject: Residency and subprocessors — confirmation needed before procurement

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed. Before procurement moves to contract, our security & privacy team needs two clarifications so we can sign the DPA addendum:

1) Can you confirm that customer data for our EU account will be processed and stored in EU-only infrastructure under normal operations? We understand there are transient analytics and cache operations; please specify whether any production tokens or request payloads could be routed to non-EU hosts (US/APAC) for inference, telemetry, or analytics.

2) We need the complete subprocessor roster (current and planned for next quarter) and the timing for any subprocessor activations. If any subprocessor is based outside EEA, please indicate the transfer mechanism (SCCs, BCRs, or another lawful basis).

Also, MedLumen has a strict temporary-failover tolerance: we can accept transient cross-region hops only for incident-driven failover (max 72 hours) with prior notice where feasible and a requirement to annotate data residency logs for audit. Can Redwood support that operational constraint in the DPA addendum?

If you prefer, loop in your legal and ops and we can set a short call. We need answers by next Wednesday (4/26) to stay on our procurement timeline.

Best,
Sophie Moreau
Head of Security, MedLumen
MedLumen B.V.
Attachments: none

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Moreau <sophie.moreau@medlumen-eu.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 09:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency and subprocessors — confirmation needed before procurement

Hi Sophie — thanks, really appreciate the clear asks and timeline. Short answers up front:

- Normal ops: yes, we can commit to EU-only placement for MedLumen production inference and persistent storage when you choose EU pinning.
- Transient processing: we may have short-lived hops for certain telemetry/analytics or incident-driven failover; we support a 72-hour temporary hop window as an operational policy with annotations in audit logs.
- Subprocessors: we’ll provide the roster and planned activations in a separate attachment and include transfer mechanism flags.

I’m looping in Kimberly (Legal) for the DPA addendum language and Marcus (Solutions) for the operational runbook. Lauren — can you help with the DocuSign workflow once Kimberly produces a redline?

I’ll follow up shortly with the roster and a drafted addendum. If helpful, we can do a quick 30-min call early next week to walk MedLumen’s procurement/legal through the clauses.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0142

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Moreau <sophie.moreau@medlumen-eu.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Apr 2028 10:05:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Residency and subprocessors — confirmation needed before procurement

Hi Sophie, Jordan —

Per Jordan’s note, attaching a draft DPA addendum that:
- Adds an explicit EU placement commitment clause when the customer selects EU pinning (persistent storage + inference shall remain within EU jurisdictional boundaries).
- Defines "Transient Processing Hop" as a limited exception for incident-driven failover, analytics backfill, or telemetry ingestion. Any transient hop must be:
  * limited to 72 consecutive hours per incident unless mutually agreed otherwise,
  * logged with start/end timestamps and hostname/region metadata,
  * surfaced in the customer audit log for at least 12 months.
- Requires Redwood to use SCCs or equivalent safeguards for transfers to subprocessors outside the EEA; planned activations must be notified 30 days prior to activation (except in emergency failover).

Attachments included: DPA_Addendum_MedLumen_v1.pdf (annotated), subprocessors_2028Q2.csv (current+planned roster with country and transfer mechanism flags).

Notes on the roster: most infra subprocessors (cloud providers) have EU regions we leverage by default; a small analytics vendor used for aggregated telemetry is US-based and will be covered via SCCs and pseudonymization of identifiers. We mark planned activations in Q2 as "conditional" — we will not enable them for your tenant without explicit activation steps and notice.

Sophie — please review the annotated addendum and roster. I included a suggested DocuSign workflow link in the cover note if you want to proceed. If you need language changes, flag them and I’ll circulate clean redlines.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: DPA_Addendum_MedLumen_v1.pdf; subprocessors_2028Q2.csv

From: Sophie Moreau <sophie.moreau@medlumen-eu.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@medlumen-eu.com
Date: Sat, 21 Apr 2028 14:47:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Residency and subprocessors — confirmation needed before procurement

Thanks Kimberly, Jordan — this is very helpful. A few quick clarifying questions before we circulate to procurement/legal:

1) The 72-hour transient hop clause — can you add an operational SLA that Redwood will provide "reasonable prior notice" for scheduled maintenance that may trigger cross-region processing? For incident-driven hops, we need an incident report within 24 hours that includes the hop start time, affected datasets, and whether any PII left the EU.

2) On the analytics vendor: can you confirm the pseudonymization approach (one-way hashing with salted keys per-tenant or tokenization) and whether raw request payloads are ever forwarded? We prefer no raw payload forwarding.

3) Regarding subprocessor notifications: MedLumen requires a 30-day activation notice for planned subprocessors and a 14-day post-activation confirmation for emergency activations. Can you accept that as part of the DPA addendum?

We can accept the addendum with those two small changes and proceed with signature via DocuSign. If you can produce a redline with those items and the drafts of the short MAP (mutual action plan) timing, we are ready to move.

Regards,
Sophie

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Moreau <sophie.moreau@medlumen-eu.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency and subprocessors — confirmation needed before procurement

Sophie — appreciate the quick review and clear asks. We can commit to the three items you called out:

- Notice & incident reporting: we will add language requiring reasonable prior notice for scheduled maintenance that could cause cross-region hops, and incident-driven hops will be accompanied by a post-incident memo within 24 hours with timestamps, affected datasets, and PII exposure confirmation (if any).
- Analytics pseudonymization: the analytics vendor will receive salted, tenant-specific one-way hashes; we will not forward raw request payloads to that vendor. I had Marcus include an ops note in the MAP draft.
- Subprocessor timing: we accept 30-day prior notice for planned activations and 14-day confirmation for emergency activations.

I’ve attached a short draft MAP (MedLumen_MAP_draft.xlsx) with milestones: DPA redline by Tue 4/23, legal sign-off by 4/25, DocuSign signature and onboarding kickoff week of 4/29.

Next steps: Kimberly will circulate a redlined addendum reflecting the three edits; Lauren will schedule the DocuSign workflow once you confirm final language. If you prefer a 30-min sync, we can do Tuesday morning CEST.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out and getting your sandbox provisioned.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | jordan.blake@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415 555 0142
Attachments: MedLumen_MAP_draft.xlsx
